swaps.name: smaller VLM box source: Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct (3.8B) for the 7B LLaVA-OneVision prior
swaps.weaker_variant: Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct (strictly fewer parameters), same prompt template; head refit on train-carved rows with the 3B boxes (deployment-consistent); measured BETTER than the 7B LLaVA boxes on all three datasets -- grounding quality here is family-limited, not size-limited
swaps.note: strictly smaller than both the incumbent 7B and the rival's cloud MLLM; head and reference both refit/rerun on train-carved rows with the 3B boxes

swaps.name: smaller proposal pool: SAM ViT-B (0.09B) for SAM ViT-H (0.64B)
swaps.weaker_variant: SAM ViT-B automatic masks (pps=8, same released thresholds), G2L features re-extracted, head refit on SAM-B train-carved rows
swaps.note: ViT-L was the first choice; the original-format ViT-L checkpoint is not reachable offline (HF port restructures the prompt encoder), so the strictly smaller ViT-B is the measured arm. Under SAM-B the learned head is within ±0.4 mIoU of the geom-only argmax pick on every dataset (mixed signs), i.e. the pool itself is the binding constraint at this strength. The head-level 0.28 margin below the floor is within unquantified single-seed refit noise; the load-bearing conclusion rests on the pool-oracle gap (79.1 -> 71.4 mIoU), which is robust. ViT-L between ViT-B and ViT-H is unmeasured (original-format checkpoint unreachable offline), so the RefCOCOg bracket is [ViT-B 57.57, ViT-H 65.51]

swaps.name: weaker region-text platform: plain masked-region CLIP (no G2L fusion, no complement blur)
swaps.weaker_variant: our own masked-region CLIP ViT-B/16 features (mask fill + resize + CLS), head refit on train-carved rows with the plain features
swaps.note: removes the released G2L fusion and complement-blur path entirely

swaps.name: gRefCOCO without the GroundingDINO detector (fewer components than the rival)
swaps.weaker_variant: detector-free realization: the training-free termbox rule with LLaVA nounboxes only. Structural note: the shipped declared-trained recipe's candidate substrate on this path is built from detector boxes and detector-box-prompted SAM masks, so removing the detector necessarily removes the trained recipe with it; no intermediate (nounbox-prompted SAM masks + transferred head) was measured, and the boundary below is therefore scoped to the detector-free realization, not to the detector in isolation
swaps.note: corrected per-record-alignment detector-free realization: base noun 38.56, per-clause 37.95, presence-filtered 37.85, sentence box 36.70, pair/union 36.73, and the 320-trial held-out searched clause config 40.56 cIoU / 70.56 gIoU; none clears the 44.4 same-class floor. The earlier 38.43/38.08/38.24/36.74 numbers used a ref_id-keyed term map and are superseded.

verdict: Scoped, component by component (full official val, aligned protocol; the reference and head were refit on train-carved rows wherever the platform or pool changed): (a) the box prior can be SMALLER AND BETTER -- Qwen2.5-VL-3B (3.8B, strictly smaller than both the 7B incumbent and the rival's cloud MLLM) holds SOTA on all three datasets and improves on the shipped boxes (73.57/67.64/66.43 vs 70.57/66.35/65.51 mIoU), so grounding quality here is family-limited, not size-limited; (c) the region-text platform can be weakened for free -- plain masked-region CLIP without the released G2L fusion or complement blur keeps full-table SOTA at -0.2..-0.4 mIoU (70.22/65.98/65.32). Two boundaries are measured and kept: (b) SAM ViT-B's pool oracle falls from 79.1 to 71.4 mIoU on RefCOCOg and the refit head lands 57.57, 0.28 BELOW the published GLOD-RIS floor -- the ViT-H pool is load-bearing there; and (d) the detector-free gRefCOCO rule scores 38.71 cIoU, below the same-class 44.4 floor -- the extra detector is load-bearing there. 2/4 swap arms still clear their floors. The detector-free boundary is scoped to the detector-free REALIZATION (training-free termbox rule): the shipped trained recipe's substrate is detector-derived, so the two cannot be separated in this arm. The gRefCOCO term-alignment correction supersedes the earlier no-detector numbers; the corrected best DINO-free arm is 40.56 cIoU, still below the same-class floor.
